In Re: 39907116 Date: NOV. 14, 2025
Appeal of Service Center Operations (SCOPS) Decision
Form I-918 - Supplement A, Petition for Qualifying Family Member of a U-1 Nonimmigrant
The Applicant, who was granted "T-1" nonimmigrant status (T-1 principal), seeks nonimmigrant
classification for his mother (the Derivative) under the Immigration and Nationality Act (the Act)
section 101(a)(15)(T)(ii), 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(15)(T)(ii). Service Center Operations (SCOPS) denied
the Form I-914 - Supplement A, Application for Qualifying Family Member of a T-1 Nonimmigrant
(T derivative application), concluding that the Applicant did not establish that the Derivative was an
eligible immediate family member. The matter is now before us on appeal. 8 C.F.R. § 103.3.
The Applicant bears the burden ofproof to demonstrate eligibility by a preponderance ofthe evidence.
Matter ofChawathe, 25 I&N Dec. 369, 375-76 (AAO 2010). We review the questions in this matter
de novo. Matter of Christo 's, Inc., 26 I&N Dec. 537, 537 n.2 (AAO 2015). Upon de novo review,
we will dismiss the appeal.
In January 2022, the Applicant filed this T derivative application and listed his mother's name as
C-M-M-O-1 . SCOPS observed that the Applicant's Honduran birth certificate indicated that his
mother's name was C-E-M-H-. Therefore, SCOPS requested that the Applicant submit documentary
evidence showing that C-M-M-O- and C-E-M-H- were the same person, including evidence of a name
change under civil authority. In response, the Applicant submitted affidavits from family members
which explained why the name was listed incorrectly and asserted that C-M-M-O-and C-E-M-H-were
the same person. In January 2025, SCOPS denied the application concluding that the Applicant's
response was insufficient.
Upon de novo review, we adopt and affirm the Director's decision with the comments below. See
Matter ofP. Singh, 26 I&N Dec. 623 (BIA 2015) (citing Matter ofBurbano, 20 I&N Dec. 872, 874
(BIA 1994); see also Chen v. INS, 87 F.3d 5, 7-8 (1st Cir. 1996) ("[I]f a reviewing tribunal decides
that the facts and evaluative judgments rescinding from them have been adequately confronted and
correctly resolved by a trial judge or hearing officer, then the tribunal is free simply to adopt those
findings" provided the tribunal's order reflects individualized attention to the case).
1 We use initials to protect the privacy of individuals.
2

On appeal, the Applicant argues that SCOPS inappropriately requested name change paperwork and
that no such documentation exists because his mother did not change her name. He explains that his
birth was not registered by his mother because she was too young to do so. Instead, his birth was
registered by his paternal grandfather who made the mistake with his mother's name. We agree with
the Applicant that if the Derivative did not change her name by civil authority, then there would be no
evidence to support such action. However, adding to the name discrepancy, the Applicant's asylum
application listed his mother's name as
C-H-M-. We determine that the Applicant has not overcome the grounds for denial.
On appeal, the Applicant indicates that he has begun the process ofconducting maternity DNA testing
and requests time to submit this additional evidence. However, to date, the Applicant has not
submitted the results of any DNA test; or indeed any evidence that the Derivative has corrected the
error on the Applicant's birth certificate through the Registro Nacional de las Personas (RNP), or other
appropriate civil authority. Hence, the Derivative remains ineligible for T nonimmigrant status under
section 101 (a)( l 5)(T) of the Act. Although we recognize the hardship that this result may cause, we
lack the authority to waive the requirements of the regulations. See United States v. Nixon, 418 U.S.
683, 695-96 (1974) (holding that both governing statutes and their implementing regulations have "the
force of law" and must be adhered to by government officials). Accordingly, the Derivative is
ineligible for classification as a derivative under section 10l(a)(l5)(T)(ii) of the Act.
ORDER: The appeal is dismissed.
NOTICE: This constitutes the final decision in this matter. The filing of a motion will not postpone
the effect of the decision. 8 C.F.R. § 103 .5( a )(1 )(iv). Aliens who are not lawfully present, or who are
otherwise inadmissible or deportable, may be subject to the commencement of removal proceedings
under section 240 of the Act through the issuance of a Form I-862, Notice to Appear. Those
proceedings may result in their removal from the United States and possible ineligibility for future
visas or other immigration benefits.
